title: Present my model and next step
subject: Design & Technology
label: Public edition
objective_verbatim: Present my product and say what I would improve.
display_objective: Present my product and say what I would improve.
calendar_note: No teaching day or clock slot is inferred.
assessment_verbatim: F: safe-working observation.  S: constructed product + evaluation (data drop).

sources.note: Current main bytes match the accepted unchanged source; workbook not redistributed.
W5 30 Nov–4 Dec; W6 7–11 Dec; W7 14–18 Dec. One lesson weekly per line; no day or slot inferred.

external_sources.title: HSE: Health and safety checklist for classrooms
external_sources.supports: The ordinary classroom checklist excludes specialist D&T; staff use activity-appropriate risk controls and local procedures.

external_sources.title: Science Buddies: Build the Best Paper Bridge
external_sources.supports: Folding a sheet into a channel can change how it resists bending. The local dimensions, light block test and stop rules are authored classroom choices; no strength result is assumed.

evidence.description: An accessible product presentation with authentic purpose/process/result, a reasoned proposed improvement, actual audience question and learner reply, with mode/support recorded.
evidence.status: contribution to source assessment; no completion claim

routes.Supported: Supported: use the sentence frames with staff.
routes.Independent: Independent: include purpose, result and change.
routes.Aspire: Aspire: answer a question about a fair retest.

vocab.definition: Share work so someone can understand it.
What something is meant to do.
The person or people receiving the message.
Words or a sign used to ask something.
What we say or do in reply.

cases.text: Choose your model or a clear work-only photo.
cases.fact: The audience needs to know the product.
cases.next_step: State whose work it is and what it was for.
cases.staff_note: A staff-made substitute must be labelled; do not claim it as pupil making.

cases.fact: The making step has an owner.
cases.next_step: Describe the step and any support.
cases.staff_note: Scribe exact learner words where needed.

cases.fact: The result should match observed work.
cases.next_step: Say what happened and when the test stopped.
cases.staff_note: Do not invent a successful test for presentation.

cases.next_step: Link it to the result and explain how it might help.
cases.staff_note: No guarantee of greater strength is made.

cases.fact: A real question needs a response.
cases.next_step: Reply, clarify it or say what needs checking.
cases.staff_note: Do not fabricate the audience question in advance as a learner result.

cases.text: Speaking to a group feels too much.
cases.fact: The presentation mode is a barrier.
cases.next_step: Use a quiet adult audience, note, pointing or AAC.
cases.staff_note: No forced performance; record the chosen mode and support.

Purpose and success checks

Safe teaching evidence and learner voice
Boundaries
No forced group presentation or video. Share work-only records under local rules. A question can be answered with “I need to check”. Do not use public uploads or personal accounts.
Assessment and feedback

Require product purpose, one actual making step with support, real test observation or honest not-tested statement, and a linked improvement. Record the real audience and exchange. Accept quiet one-to-one, notes, pointing or AAC. A prepared script without an audience exchange is preparation, not evidence of a delivered presentation.

Retain actual work, response mode and support. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence in the school's evidence record). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after evidence is banked. Blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Lundy moments
Space: calm, accessible participation. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Speaking listening and writing

Present an explanation, listen to a question and give a reasoned response; receiving staff map authentic evidence to their own portfolio. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own portfolio; no communication criteria are assigned here.

Model and hinge

Fictional example: My model is a card bridge. I folded the sides; an adult held the ruler. The test note says the centre bent. I would try a folded edge to support the centre. Question: Will it hold any load? Reply: I cannot say. A fair retest could check the proposed change.

B. An improvement is a reasoned proposal until it is checked. A and C overclaim strength. Ask the learner to link the proposal to an observed result, then say how a later comparable test could check it. No new load test is required in this lesson.
Individual evidence key

Require product purpose, one actual making step with support, real test observation or honest not-tested statement, and a linked improvement. Record the real audience and exchange. Accept quiet one-to-one, notes, pointing or AAC. A prepared script without an audience exchange is preparation, not evidence of a delivered presentation.
Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: A staff-made substitute must be labelled; do not claim it as pupil making.
Card B: Scribe exact learner words where needed.
Card C: Do not invent a successful test for presentation.
Card D: No guarantee of greater strength is made.
Card E: Do not fabricate the audience question in advance as a learner result.
Card F: No forced performance; record the chosen mode and support.
Common misunderstandings
Presenting need not mean public speaking. An honest limit is stronger evidence than an invented success. An improvement remains a proposal until tested.
Teaching boundary
No forced group presentation or video. Share work-only records under local rules. A question can be answered with “I need to check”. Do not use public uploads or personal accounts.
Feedback

If a reason is missing, return to the fact or actual work. Re-model a different example, then keep the learner’s own revision. Use NS+ and the learner response in their own colour before R. E means evidence actually banked. Keep safeguarding records separate.
